title: Choose how Mezzanine's first run is laid out
question: Three layouts for onboarding (sign in, server, profile, library warm-up). The world is set; this picks the composition.

options.label: Express
options.thesis: One button does it all: sign in, pick the fastest server, read the library — then shows what it chose, with Change links.
options.viewport: MEZZANINE title card on the gutter, one line, one lilac 'Sign In with Plex'. After approval the same column fills with three settled facts (account, server via LAN, library 5,616 titles) each with Change, while posters fade in behind.
options.risk: Hides choices the wife's profile pick needs; Change links must be obvious.

options.label: One Page
options.thesis: Every step on one page, top to bottom; each unlocks when the one above is done, and stays visible as a record.
options.viewport: Numbered rows down the gutter column: 1 Sign in (active, lilac button), 2 Server (dim), 3 Profile (dim), 4 Library (dim). Done rows collapse to one ruled caption line with a check.
options.risk: Reads like a form; the least cinematic of the three.

options.label: Poster Wall
options.thesis: Your own library is the welcome: as the index reads, posters fill a wall across the window and the room takes their light; steps sit in a column at the left.
options.viewport: Left 40%: graphite column with the current step (title, one line, one control). Right 60%: a tilted-free grid of your posters appearing as they sync, dimmed until the last step, then fully lit as Home opens.
options.risk: The wall needs a signed-in account; before sign-in it is empty, so step one leans on the title alone.
